title: Precision Ocular Biometry: Optical vs. Ultrasound
summary: Mastering the gold standards of axial length measurement is fundamental to modern refractive surgery and intraocular lens power calculations. This guide delineates the physical, clinical, and technological distinctions between Immersion/Contact Ultrasound and Optical Low-Coherence Interferometry.

sections.title: The IOL Power Formula Imperative
content: Axial Length (AL) error of 1mm = ~2.5 to 3.0 D of IOL power error.
Optical biometry is the gold standard for modern formulas (Barrett Universal II, Hill-RBF, Kane).
Ultrasound remains the fallback for dense cataracts where laser light cannot reach the RPE.

branches: Optical: Routine phaco, Refractive lens exchange, Post-LASIK (if topography available)
Contact US: Dense PSC/Nuclear cataracts, Corneal opacity, Vitreous hemorrhage
Immersion US: Superior to contact (avoids compression artifact)

sections.title: Red Flags: Avoiding 'IOL Surprise'
content: Corneal compression during contact A-scan (leads to falsely short AL).
Poor fixation during optical biometry (leads to decentered measurement).
Failure to account for silicone oil (requires specialized velocity settings in US).
Inaccurate velocity settings (standard: 1550m/s for phakic eyes, 1532m/s for aphakic).
Anisometropia > 0.3mm difference between eyes without clinical explanation.

sections.title: Diagnostic Protocol: Ultrasound
content: Step 1: Topical anesthesia (Proparacaine).
Step 2: Ensure perpendicular probe alignment (maximize echo spikes).
Step 3: Immersion shell placement (Prager shell) to prevent compression.
Step 4: Capture 5-10 readings; discard outliers.
Step 5: Verify standard deviation < 0.1mm.

sections.title: Diagnostic Protocol: Optical
content: Step 1: Patient alignment (chin rest, fixation light).
Step 2: Automated signal peak acquisition.
Step 3: Check SNR (Signal-to-Noise Ratio) > 2.0.
Step 4: If poor signal due to cataract, repeat 3-5 times.
Step 5: Compare K-readings with manual keratometry if discrepant.

content.explanation: O: Optical (Laser); P: Precise (micron-level); T: Tissue (RPE target); I: Interferometry; C: Cataract-limited (requires optical clarity).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always measure the fellow eye to confirm symmetry.
In staphylomatous eyes, optical biometry may target the fovea rather than the absolute posterior pole.
Immersion ultrasound is significantly more accurate than contact ultrasound because it eliminates indentation.
Post-refractive surgery: Use Barrett True-K or Hill-RBF with clinical history method as a check.
Always verify the IOL formula constants (A-constant) are optimized for the specific biometer used.
